questions.q: A report says "Demand has been rising since January" and the reporting period is still ongoing. Which interpretation fits this wording?
options: The upward movement began in January and has continued into the current period.
The upward movement is scheduled to start in a future January.
The upward movement ended before January began.
The sentence states only January’s final demand level, without describing a movement.
questions.explanation: Has been rising since links an ongoing process with its starting point. It is not a forecast or merely a statement of the level at one date.

questions.q: Which phrase correctly completes "The report records ___ demand for the service", when the writer means that demand became lower?
options: a decline at
a decline in
a declining of
a decline to
questions.explanation: A decline in demand names the variable that became lower. A decline of normally introduces an amount; a decline to introduces the level reached.

questions.q: Sales rose for several months and then stayed close to the same level. Which expression best describes this final phase?
options: Sales accelerated.
Sales reversed their upward trend and fell.
Sales levelled off.
Sales continued rising at an increasing rate.
questions.explanation: Levelled off describes a movement becoming broadly flat after an increase or decrease. It differs from acceleration or reversal into a decline.

questions.q: Orders increased by 9.8%. Which description retains that figure’s proximity to 10% without placing it above 10%?
options: Orders increased by just over 10%.
Orders increased by at least 10%.
Orders increased by no less than 10%.
Orders increased by just under 10%.
questions.explanation: Just under places the figure slightly below the reference value. Just over, at least and no less than place it above or at that value.

questions.q: The source reports “an increase of 5% over the full two-year period”. A summary calls it “5% every year”. What has been altered?
options: The period to which the growth rate applies
The currency in which the figures are reported
The distinction between gross and net profit
The identity of the reporting company
questions.explanation: Un taux cumulé sur deux ans n’est pas un taux à appliquer chaque année. La reformulation doit conserver la durée à laquelle la variation se rapporte.

questions.q: A report gives a percentage increase in units sold but no selling-price information. Which description stays within the evidence?
options: The average selling price increased by that percentage.
The volume of units sold increased.
Sales revenue increased by the same percentage.
Net profit increased by the same percentage.
questions.explanation: Une hausse des quantités renseigne sur le volume. Sans prix et sans coûts, elle ne fixe ni la croissance du chiffre d’affaires ni celle du bénéfice.

questions.q: Revenue fell from €100,000 to €80,000 and then rose to €90,000. Which wording accurately describes the last movement?
options: Revenue recovered fully to its initial level.
Revenue reached a new high above its initial level.
Revenue recovered partially but remained below its initial level.
Revenue continued falling from its intermediate low.
questions.explanation: Recovered partially describes a rise after the fall that does not restore the starting level. The final €90,000 is between the low and the initial €100,000.

questions.q: Actual output was 105 units against a target of 100. Which wording accurately states performance against the target?
options: Output fell short of the target.
Output exactly met the target.
Output was capped at the target.
Output exceeded the target.
questions.explanation: Exceed means to be above the reference. Fall short means to be below, and exactly meet means equality; a cap is a limit rather than the reported excess.

questions.q: A source says “sales peaked at €3 million in May”. Which summary preserves both the level and its status?
options: Sales reached their highest reported level of €3 million in May.
Sales increased by exactly €3 million in May.
Sales remained at €3 million throughout the year.
Sales will peak at €3 million next May.
questions.explanation: Peaked at désigne un maximum observé. Il ne donne pas à lui seul le montant de l’augmentation, une stabilité annuelle ou une prévision future.

questions.q: A chart labels its final observation “€7m”. Which wording preserves the unit when describing that level?
options: Revenue rose by seven percentage points over the period.
Revenue ended the period at seven million euros.
Revenue ended the period at seven thousand euros.
Revenue rose by seven percent over the period.
questions.explanation: Le symbole m correspond ici à million, et at décrit le niveau. Passer à milliers, à un taux ou à des points modifie la mesure.

questions.q: Monthly orders moved sharply up and down, although their annual average was close to last year’s. Which description preserves both features?
options: Orders were stable in every month because the annual average was unchanged.
Orders declined steadily throughout the year because some months were lower.
Orders were volatile during the year despite a broadly unchanged annual average.
Orders rose steadily throughout the year because some months were higher.
questions.explanation: Volatile describes the pronounced fluctuations. A stable annual average does not imply that each observation was stable or followed one steady direction.

questions.q: A production report gives a target of 80 units and actual output of 70 units. Which summary preserves the status of the figures?
options: Actual output reached 80 units.
The target was revised down to 70 units.
The target guarantees 80 units next year.
Actual output was below the target.
questions.explanation: Une cible et un constat sont deux informations différentes. Le résultat de 70 unités reste inférieur à la cible de 80 ; aucun changement de cible ni résultat futur garanti n’est indiqué.

questions.q: Profit fell "by up to 8%" across the divisions studied. Which statement preserves the limit expressed by "up to"?
options: The decline is described as no greater than 8%; the wording does not require every division to have declined by exactly 8%.
Every division necessarily recorded exactly the same 8% decline.
Each division recorded a decline of at least 8%.
The combined profit margin necessarily finished at 8%.
questions.explanation: Up to states an upper limit in this description. It does not give a minimum, a common value for every division or the final margin.

questions.q: A market report states that "sales tripled". Which comparison does that expression describe?
options: The final sales level was the initial level plus 3%.
The final sales level was three times the initial level.
The final sales level was four times the initial level.
The final sales level was one third of the initial level.
questions.explanation: Tripled means that the final level equals three times the initial level. It is not a three-percent increase or an addition of three times the starting level.

questions.q: A report correctly states that a margin rose by four percentage points. A headline changes this to “profit rose by four percent”. What is wrong?
options: Percentage points always measure the growth of total profit.
The original statement already gave the total profit amount.
Both the indicator and the type of change have been altered.
Only the language has changed; the financial meaning is identical.
questions.explanation: La marge est un ratio, tandis que le profit est un montant. En outre, un écart en points ne se confond pas avec une hausse relative du bénéfice.

questions.q: A report says that rising service revenue "offset the fall in product revenue" and total revenue was unchanged. What did the service increase do?
options: It caused an additional decline of the same size in total revenue.
It converted the product-revenue decline into a decline in costs.
It left total revenue lower by the full amount of the product-revenue decline.
It compensated for the product-revenue decline in the total.
questions.explanation: Offset means to counterbalance another movement. In this case the stated unchanged total makes the compensating role explicit.

questions.q: A table labels a margin movement “pp”. A translator expands this as “percentage profits”. Which expansion is correct?
options: Percentage points
Payment periods
Price per product
Profit payments
questions.explanation: Dans un tableau de variation de taux ou de marges, pp abrège percentage points. Percentage profits n’est pas l’intitulé de cette unité.

questions.q: The report says that subscription services "accounted for 30% of revenue". What does this phrase describe?
options: The rate at which subscription revenue increased during the year.
The share of total revenue generated by subscription services.
The share of subscription revenue remaining after its costs were deducted.
The amount by which total revenue exceeded its previous level.
questions.explanation: Accounted for describes a contribution to a total here, not a growth rate or margin. The denominator is total revenue.

questions.q: A seasonal business compares December sales with November sales. Which additional comparison would help distinguish seasonal patterns from year-on-year performance?
options: December sales with the same year’s annual total alone, treated as an equivalent monthly reference.
December sales with an unrelated low-season month, without controlling the seasonal difference.
December sales with December sales in the previous year
December sales with the average of January and February alone, treated as a year-on-year comparison.
questions.explanation: Une comparaison avec le même mois de l’année précédente aide à tenir compte de la saisonnalité. Elle doit néanmoins conserver le même périmètre et les mêmes unités.

questions.q: Costs fell while sales remained stable. Which connecting expression accurately contrasts the two observations?
options: Costs fell because sales remained stable, making the contrast a stated causal explanation.
Costs fell only if sales remained stable, making the contrast a condition.
Costs fell so that sales would remain stable, making the contrast a purpose.
Costs fell, whereas sales remained stable.
questions.explanation: Whereas marque un contraste sans ajouter une cause. Des ventes stables et des coûts en baisse peuvent être rapportés ensemble sans surinterprétation.

questions.q: A chart reports growth "year to date" at the end of September. Which period does this expression normally cover in a calendar-year report?
options: From the beginning of the current year through the September reporting date.
September alone compared with August.
The twelve months ending in September, regardless of the start of the current year.
The completed previous calendar year only.
questions.explanation: Year to date refers to the elapsed part of the current reporting year. It differs from month-on-month, a rolling twelve-month period and the previous full year.

questions.q: A report gives a forecast for next quarter and actual figures for the current quarter. Which summary makes the distinction clear?
options: The current figures are hypothetical because a forecast is also shown.
Current figures are observed; next-quarter figures remain projections.
Both sets of figures are completed historical results.
The forecast guarantees next quarter’s outcome.
questions.explanation: Le fait qu’un document réunisse constat et prévision ne change pas le statut de chaque série. Le commentaire doit préserver cette distinction temporelle et probatoire.

questions.q: A writer compares nominal sales growth with a constant-price growth figure as if both measured the same change. Which issue should be disclosed?
options: The shared percentage sign establishes that both figures use an identical price basis.
Both growth figures necessarily remove the effect of changing prices because each compares two periods.
The price basis differs between the two measures.
The nominal figure can be treated as a volume measure without checking whether price changes were removed.
questions.explanation: Une mesure à prix constants vise à neutraliser un effet de prix, contrairement à une évolution nominale. Le même symbole % ne rend pas les bases équivalentes.
